scenes.headline: How plants eat *light*
scenes.sub: Every calorie you have ever eaten began as sunlight caught by a leaf.

items.title: Carbon dioxide
items.detail: Drawn in through *stomata* — microscopic pores on the underside of the leaf.

items.title: Water
items.detail: Pulled up from the roots through the xylem, against gravity, all day long.

items.title: Light energy
items.detail: Absorbed by *chlorophyll*, which reflects green — that is why leaves look green.

items.title: Light reactions — in the thylakoid
items.detail: Light splits water. Oxygen leaves as waste; energy is banked as *ATP and NADPH*.

items.title: Calvin cycle — in the stroma
items.detail: That banked energy fixes CO₂ into sugar. No light needed here, only the products of stage one.
